summary: Independent adversarial code review of issue-9: REQUEST-CHANGES. The terms gate itself is correct, server-authoritative, contract-adherent across all 13 interfaces, and fully green (tsc, 39/39 vitest, lint, format:check, next build all pass). Five substantive findings: (1) High - src/lib/db.ts creates a pg Pool with no 'error' listener, so an idle-client backend/network error emits an unhandled EventEmitter 'error' and crashes the Node process (verified in pg-pool 8.23.0 index.js:62); (2) Medium - a CURRENT_TERMS_VERSION rollback permanently locks a teacher out of uploads in a silent success loop, because hasAcceptedCurrentTerms uses 'latest row wins' instead of an existence check while recordAcceptance swallows 23505 as success; (3) Medium - recordAcceptance returns a fabricated in-memory acceptedAt on the 23505 path that matches no stored row, undermining the ticket's core auditability criterion; (4) Medium/latent - POST /api/terms-acceptance has no CSRF, Origin, or Content-Type validation, and request.json() does not enforce Content-Type, so a text/plain cross-origin form can forge a legally binding acceptance once issue #2 lands cookie sessions; (5) Medium - getAcceptanceStatus collapses 'never accepted' and 'accepted an older version' into a bare {accepted:false}, so after a version bump the settings page tells a teacher who did accept that they never accepted, breaking the 'review the accepted terms version in settings' success criterion. Findings 2, 3 and 5 are inherited from contract Interfaces 4 and 10, not coder deviations, and need a contract amendment alongside the code fix. No unauthorized contract deviations were found; the two behavioral divergences (request.json().catch for malformed bodies, and a submitting double-submit guard on the modal) are safe supersets of the locked behavior.

commands_run: git --no-pager diff main...HEAD -- src/ migrations/ .env.example README.md package.json vitest.config.ts
verification.notes: All repository quality gates pass independently: tsc --noEmit exit 0; vitest 14 files / 39 tests all green (this includes the meta-tests that run npm run lint, npm run format:check, and npm run build); next build succeeds. all_passed is false because the review itself returns REQUEST-CHANGES on code-quality grounds, not because any command failed. Finding 1 was verified against the installed pg-pool source rather than inferred. Finding 4's text/plain CSRF vector was reasoned from the fact that Request.json() performs no Content-Type check. next build output confirmed /settings and /upload are prerendered static (a latent, self-correcting note, not a finding). No code files were modified during this review.

follow_ups: CR-01 (required before merge, High): Attach a pool.on("error", ...) handler in src/lib/db.ts getPool() so an idle-client error cannot crash the Node process.

CR-02 (required before merge, Medium): Validate Content-Type is application/json and/or check Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site on POST /api/terms-acceptance, or record it as a tracked hard prerequisite on issue #2 before any cookie-based session ships.

CR-03 (contract amendment + code, Medium): Replace the 'latest acceptance row' predicate in src/lib/terms-acceptance.ts with an existence check on (teacher_id, CURRENT_TERMS_VERSION); amend contract Interface 4. Also add a deterministic tiebreak (ORDER BY accepted_at DESC, id DESC) wherever a genuine most-recent ordering is still required.

CR-04 (contract amendment + code, Medium): Use INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (teacher_id, terms_version) DO UPDATE ... RETURNING accepted_at so recordAcceptance always returns the persisted timestamp instead of new Date().toISOString(); amend contract Interface 4.

CR-05 (contract amendment + code, Medium): Extend AcceptanceStatus with the latest acceptance's version/timestamp regardless of currency so src/app/settings/page.tsx can distinguish 'never accepted' from 'accepted an older version'; amend contract Interfaces 4 and 10.

CR-06 (low): Add tests for the contract-locked 401 unauthenticated paths on GET/POST /api/terms-acceptance and a direct unit test for getAcceptanceStatus - both still open from spec-review SR-01 and SR-05.
CR-07 (low): Consider export const dynamic = "force-dynamic" on /upload and /settings, and a globalThis-cached pool singleton in src/lib/db.ts to avoid a Pool leak per dev HMR reload.
open_questions: Findings 2, 3 and 5 originate in contract.md Interfaces 4 and 10 rather than in the implementation. Should the contract be reopened and amended in this ticket, or should these be split into a follow-up ticket so issue-9 can ship with only CR-01 and CR-02 fixed?

Is deferring the CSRF/Content-Type hardening (CR-02) to issue #2 acceptable to the human gate, given that the endpoint writes the ticket's legal-evidence record and is unprotected the instant real session auth lands?
